article.title: September 2026 (Volume 78, Number 4)
article.author: Jamil Jonna
article.content: Taking as a starting point two classic works of the mid-nineteenth century—Benjamin Disraeli’s Sybil; or the Two Nations and Frederick Engels’s The Condition of the Working Class in England —this month’s “Notes from the Editors” explores the way both authors articulated the plight of workers in their own era, drawing key parallels to our own time. The similarities are particularly conspicuous when examining the so-called affordability crisis, exposing the regime of social murder that accompanies the increasing polarization of economic life.
